content.text:
Audit result: mobile already parses many streamed tool-call shapes, but it has no tool declarations, executor, continuation transcript, or result submission. Today a function-only response is treated as an error, so this is trace-only, not a usable tool loop. The system prompt explicitly says this at [system-prompt.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/system-prompt.ts:5).

High-priority correctness gaps:

- [`buildProviderRequest`](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:165) never sends `tools`; it accepts only `ChatMessage[]`, which cannot represent provider tool-result messages.
- [`streamCompletion`](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:555) emits calls but returns only text. A call-only stream reaches `wholePayloadFallback` with concatenated SSE, then throws “without readable text” ([lines 611–619](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:611)).
- Non-stream extraction also throws for a valid tool-only provider turn ([lines 313–344](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:313)).
- [`KeatingProvider`](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:481) records `tool-call` trace events only; it invokes no tool and creates no `tool-result`, although the shared contract supports both.
- Do not use the display-safe `contractId()` as the native provider ID: it rewrites characters ([lines 175–178](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/state/KeatingProvider.tsx:175)). Keep exact provider call IDs in a private, per-active-turn native transcript; use the normalized ID only for trace/event storage.
- `parsedToolArguments()` converts malformed JSON to `{unparsed: ...}`. Never execute that as valid arguments; validate against the declared schema and return a tool error instead.
- The 40-message slice is unsafe for tool state: never split an assistant tool-call message from its matching result, and Gemini needs the original returned function-call part (including thought signature).

Recommended shape: change the lower layer from `Promise<string>` to a provider-neutral `ProviderTurn { text, calls, usage, stopReason, nativeResponse }`; retain existing `ProviderToolCall` and `AgentStreamEvent` for UI tracing. Use a canonical `ToolDefinition`/executor registry and provider-specific request/history adapters. Run at most 4 model rounds, cap calls/results/bytes, validate before execution, give each executor the same abort signal plus timeout, and append a `tool-result` event for every call. Preserve execution results/idempotency by native call ID so retries never repeat an already successful side effect. For mutating tools, either force one-at-a-time or require explicit user confirmation.

Provider wire contracts:

| Provider | Initial declaration + turn extraction | Continuation |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Responses | `tools: [{type:"function", name, description, parameters, strict:true}]`; non-stream: `output[]` items where `type:"function_call"`, extract `call_id`, `name`, JSON-string `arguments`. Streaming: existing parser covers `response.output_item.added`, argument deltas, and `output_item.done` ([provider-client.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:475)); also retain the completed response ID and output items. | `POST /responses` with `previous_response_id: response.id` and `input: [{type:"function_call_output", call_id, output: JSON.stringify(result)}]` (one per call). Keeping `previous_response_id` within the loop avoids manually reconstructing response/reasoning items. If manually replaying history, retain the complete raw output, including reasoning items. |
| Anthropic Messages | `tools: [{name, description, input_schema}]`; usually `tool_choice:{type:"auto"}`; set `disable_parallel_tool_use:true` only when tools cannot safely run in parallel. Non-stream: `stop_reason:"tool_use"` and all `content[]` `tool_use` blocks. Streaming: current assembly of `content_block_start` + `input_json_delta` + `content_block_stop` is the right base ([lines 458–473](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:458)); also collect the exact whole assistant content and final `stop_reason`. | Append the exact assistant content, then a `user` message whose content is only every `{type:"tool_result", tool_use_id, content: JSON.stringify(result), is_error?:true}`. Keep the same tools. Tool results must immediately follow the assistant call and precede any text. [Anthropic’s tool loop](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls) documents these ordering rules. |
| Gemini `generateContent` | Root `tools:[{functionDeclarations:[{name,description,parameters}]}]`, root `toolConfig:{functionCallingConfig:{mode:"AUTO"}}`; extract every `candidates[0].content.parts[].functionCall` (not only the first). Current stream parser already walks all parts ([lines 491–497](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:491)). | Append the exact returned model `content` part(s), then `{role:"user", parts:[{functionResponse:{name, id, response:{result}}}]}`. Gemini 3 requires the exact call `id`; never fabricate `google-call-*`. Preserve the raw returned part and `thoughtSignature`, or later tool turns can fail/degrade. [Gemini’s legacy generateContent guidance](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/function-calling?authuser=1&hl=en) specifies this replay and ID behavior. |
| OpenAI-compatible / OpenRouter Chat Completions | `tools:[{type:"function",function:{name,description,parameters}}]`, `tool_choice:"auto"`; optionally `parallel_tool_calls:false`. Non-stream: `choices[0].message.tool_calls`, with `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`. Streaming: current `delta.tool_calls` index reassembly is a good base ([lines 499–513](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:499)); retain the final assistant `message`, including `tool_calls`. | Append that exact `assistant` message, then one `{role:"tool", tool_call_id:id, content:JSON.stringify(result)}` per call; reissue with tools. This is OpenRouter’s documented three-step contract. Custom endpoints must be capability-gated: “OpenAI-compatible” does not guarantee tools, streaming tool deltas, or `tool` role support. [OpenRouter guide](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/tool-calling). |

Streaming/error/usage requirements:

- Complete a tool call only on a provider terminal event/complete response, not when partial JSON first parses. If a stream ends mid-call or context/max-output truncates it, emit a retryable/error result; do not execute.
- Capture provider terminal conditions: Responses `response.failed` is already handled, but add `response.incomplete`; Anthropic `message_stop`/`stop_reason`; Gemini candidate `finishReason`; compatible/OpenRouter `choices[0].finish_reason === "error"` and nested `choices[0].error`. OpenRouter can return provider errors inside a 200 final payload, not only top-level HTTP errors. [OpenRouter error behavior](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/errors-and-debugging).
- Keep cancellation live through tool execution and follow-up request. On cancellation, do not silently drop recorded calls/results; present a recoverable cancelled state and never auto-replay mutating calls.
- `mergeProviderUsage()` using max is appropriate for cumulative events from one request. Across tool rounds, sum completed request usage—each request is billable and reprocesses context—then attach the total to the final assistant turn.
- Flush the `TextDecoder`/SSE tail at EOF; the current parser ignores a final event without a blank-line separator.
- Provider tool calls may coexist with text; retain tool-round text in trace/internal history, but only commit a learner-facing final answer after the loop reaches a non-tool terminal turn.

Tests needed:

1. Request fixtures asserting exact declarations and all four continuation envelopes, including multiple parallel calls and tool error results.
2. Non-stream tool-only and mixed text+tool responses for each provider; `requestCompletion`/stream should return a structured turn, not throw.
3. Fragmented stream fixtures: OpenAI item/delta/done, Anthropic JSON deltas, Gemini all-parts / exact ID, compatible index interleaving; duplicate frames must not execute twice.
4. End-to-end two- and four-round loops: call → result → call → final, usage summed, trace has ordered call/result pairs, final display contains only final teaching output.
5. Abort while waiting for provider, running a tool, and sending continuation; ensure no duplicate side effect on retry.
6. Invalid JSON/schema, unknown tool, timeout, executor exception, truncation, OpenRouter HTTP-200 error, and no-body/non-SSE provider responses.
7. History tests proving Anthropic adjacency, Gemini thought-signature preservation, and that truncation never separates a tool request/result pair.
